title: A proper flat space finitely presented over a dense open extends to finite presentation in codimension controlled by the boundary
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter spaces-more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms of Spaces)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file spaces-more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
difficulty_reason: Let S be a scheme, X a proper flat algebraic space over S of finite presentation, and j : U -> S a dense open such that the restriction X_U -> U is finite; the lemma concludes there is a dense open V of S containing U (in fact containing the generic points) over which X_V -> V is finite. The retained proof is written: the locus where a proper map is quasi-finite is open (cited Morphisms of Spaces, lemma proper-quasi-finite-locus-open type reference), quasi-finite proper over a locally Noetherian-ish base context gives finiteness after shrinking via the chapter's representability facts for finite maps of spaces, and the dense-open bookkeeping uses that X -> S is of finite presentation so the image of the non-finite locus is closed of empty interior by the constructibility/closedness inputs cited; the generic fibres land over U by hypothesis, which is what kills the boundary. Retained author proof at lines 8633-8646.
